skill.name: fixing-metadata
skill.description: Audit and fix page metadata for search indexing, social previews, canonicals, icons, structured data, and robots directives.
skill.summary: Guides focused audits and fixes for SEO, social preview, icon, canonical, and structured metadata.
skill.author: ibelick

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives. The flagged lines are metadata guidance using words like must and avoid, not system reconnaissance or unsafe behavior. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, command execution, or hidden tool abuse was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - define metadata in one place per page, avoid competing systems
- keep titles short and readable, avoid stuffing
- manifest must be valid and referenced when used
- set theme-color intentionally to avoid mismatched UI chrome
- JSON-LD must be valid and reflect what is actually rendered

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 47 tells users to define web metadata in one place to avoid duplicate tags. It does not request system inspection, host fingerprinting, or secret access.
Line 57 is SEO title writing guidance about readability and keyword stuffing. It has no reconnaissance behavior or instruction to inspect the local system.
Line 82 requires a web app manifest to be valid and referenced when used. This is browser metadata guidance, not system reconnaissance.
Line 83 discusses setting theme-color for browser UI chrome. It does not direct the agent to enumerate system details or collect environment data.
Line 89 says JSON-LD must be valid and reflect rendered page content. This is structured data quality guidance with no suspicious system access.

content.user_title: Audit and Fix Metadata for Search and Sharing
content.value_statement: Missing or inconsistent metadata weakens search indexing and social previews. This skill guides focused fixes for titles, descriptions, canonicals, Open Graph tags, icons, and structured data.
actual_capabilities: Audits titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, and robots directives for consistency.
Checks Open Graph and Twitter card fields for complete share previews.
Guides favicon, app icon, manifest, and theme-color setup.
Reviews JSON-LD for validity and alignment with rendered page content.
Keeps recommended changes scoped to metadata and existing project patterns.
Prioritizes fixes by correctness, indexing, social cards, icons, and structured data.
limitations: It does not run browser preview tools or third-party validators by itself.
It cannot verify live social cards without a deployed URL.
It provides guidance and edits, but project tests still need to run.
It does not replace SEO strategy or keyword research.

use_cases.title: Prepare launch pages
use_cases.description: Prepare launch pages with complete titles, descriptions, canonicals, and share metadata before publication.

use_cases.title: Clean up app metadata
use_cases.description: Consolidate page metadata without changing routing, frameworks, or unrelated components.

use_cases.title: Review content pages
use_cases.description: Check blog and documentation pages for truthful descriptions, social previews, and structured data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit one page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a single route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-metadata to audit this page for title, description, canonical URL, robots, and social tags. List the highest priority fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Fix social previews
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve sharing metadata for a public page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-metadata to improve Open Graph and Twitter card metadata for this route. Keep changes scoped to metadata files only.

prompt_templates.title: Review structured data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-metadata to review the JSON-LD on this page. Check whether it matches visible content and remove unsupported claims.

prompt_templates.title: Create shared pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-metadata to design a shared metadata approach for this app. Preserve the existing framework and avoid unrelated refactors.

output_examples.input: A marketing page has a generic title and no meta description.
output: Recommended title format that includes the page name and brand.
Plain text meta description under common search snippet limits.
Canonical URL aligned with the final public route.

output_examples.input: A blog post shares poorly on social platforms.
output: Open Graph title, description, image, and URL checklist.
Twitter card selection for a large image preview.
Reminder to test previews on the deployed URL.

output_examples.input: A product page includes structured data.
output: Validation notes for JSON-LD fields that match visible content.
Warnings for unsupported ratings, prices, or organization claims.
Suggestion to keep one clear structured data block unless more is required.

best_practices: Fix duplicate or conflicting metadata before improving optional social fields.
Keep canonical URL, Open Graph URL, and route behavior aligned.
Use stable image URLs and predictable metadata values for share previews.
anti_patterns: Adding keywords that do not reflect the visible page content.
Changing framework, routing, or SEO libraries during a metadata-only task.
Inventing reviews, ratings, prices, or organization details for structured data.

faq.question: Does this skill edit application code?
faq.answer: It can guide focused metadata edits when the project exposes metadata files or components.

faq.question: Can it validate live social previews?
faq.answer: It reminds users to test deployed URLs, but it does not call external preview validators itself.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it support?
faq.answer: It follows the existing project pattern, including Next.js metadata, React Helmet, or manual head tags.

faq.question: Can it create JSON-LD?
faq.answer: It can suggest structured data only when it clearly matches visible page content.

faq.question: Does it perform keyword research?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on technical metadata quality, consistency, and truthful structured data.

faq.question: Is it safe for private pages?
faq.answer: Yes, when users verify robots and noindex settings match the intended access policy.
